recap.workouts:
Three pieces today and all three landed.

06:00 Lodgepole — 93:20 in the gym, average heart rate 109, max 153, load 34, RPE 6. You built the cleans to 185 and stopped there, took 15 cal on the echo bike instead of the 200 m run because you were in lifting shoes, and did 2 muscle-ups per set.

On the 225: you are right and I was wrong. Your own log has 195 lb on the clean and jerk from 5 August, so 225 sat thirty pounds above your best single — written as the eighth set of a workout carrying 1600 m of running. That number came straight off the app's TRAIN column and I passed it through without checking it against your record. 185 was the correct ceiling and you found it without me.

Leg day, maintenance dose, and three of the four movements moved:
- Belt squat 100 x 12, then 110 x 11. You cleared the trigger on set one and promoted yourself mid-session. Right read — 110 is the load now.
- Leg extension 95 x 12 / 12. Trigger fired, 100 lb is earned. Week 12 is the deload, so Sunday's plan-gen decides whether that gets applied or banked.
- Leg curl 50 x 12 / 12. This came in at 11/11 two sessions running, below the range floor, with a standing note that another miss would drop the load to 45 rather than move the range. It didn't. That watch is off.
- Tibia raise 20 x 18, up from 15 last week; the second set went in without a rep count. You logged that the tibia felt harder today — 18 reps says otherwise. The trigger is 20/20 for 25 lb and you are two reps away.

CF10 — 60:08, average 171 W, max 197 W, average heart rate 132, ceiling 150, cadence 87, load 51, compliance 96%. And it paired. This morning's check flagged that no planned event existed for today and the block would land unpaired with no compliance figure; you pushed the file to the calendar before you rode. That is the difference between a measurement and a ride.

The reference block is there and it is clean. Reading the power stream directly, there is exactly one continuous run of watts in the 160-169 band in the whole session, and it lasts between 560 and 620 seconds. Ten minutes held inside a 10 W window, unbroken, nothing interrupting it. That is the block executed exactly as written, and it is the second observation in the deliberate series.

The rest of the hour did its job too. Maximum power for the entire 60 minutes was 197 W. Zone X starts at 196. So the whole session sat at or under the top of Zone 2 — an easy ride actually ridden easy, the day after ninety minutes of running and on the deepest Form reading of the block.

Against 10 August's CF10, same code, same block: 167 W at 130 bpm then, 171 W at 132 bpm today. Watts per beat 1.285 then, 1.295 now. Seven days apart, that is the same ride twice — which is what it should be. This block answers over months, not weeks. The one thing that did move: session decoupling read minus 1.6% today against plus 1.3% last Monday, meaning heart rate held or fell relative to power across the hour instead of creeping up.

Method note, stated rather than implied: the Drive folder again did not mount into the compute sandbox, so this is activity-level analysis plus a direct scan of the power stream rather than a per-second window pass. The heart rate trace inside the 165 W block specifically was not computed here — progress.py reads it at 05:57 tomorrow.
recap.takeaways:
1) Endurance verdict: EXECUTED, proceed. 96% compliance, the reference block held unbroken for its full ten minutes, not one second above Zone 2 across the hour, heart rate coupled to power. There is no fatigue flag anywhere in this trace and nothing to protect against. Confidence: high on the execution read, medium on the week-to-week comparison, because two observations seven days apart cannot separate fitness from room temperature.

2) The 225 was my error and the fix is procedural, not motivational. The class overlay copies the app's TRAIN loads straight through; your actual maxes live in your logs. When a posted load sits above a number you have genuinely lifted, the posted load is wrong for you rather than aspirational — and you applied that rule this morning without being asked. I will check the column against your log before I recommend a load again.

3) ADAPT: no-op. Endurance EXECUTED at 96%, the class MODIFIED and correctly so (load capped at your true max, echo bike for the run in lifting shoes, muscle-ups halved), hypertrophy complete at the maintenance dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves, and three load triggers fired on legs — that is not the profile of a week that needs defending.

4) The reference block is still aimed at a gate that will reject it. At 05:57 tomorrow progress.py reads today's ride, and under the current eligibility rule a CF-family stepped-ERG session lands in class_stepped_erg — the same bucket that took 10 August. That would be three collected-and-set-aside observations while the eligible 160-169 W bin stays at two old CF9 rides. This was raised on Sunday and it is still your call: relaxing an eligibility gate to admit my own measurement is exactly the move that should require your sign-off. It wants an answer before the series grows another excluded observation.
recap.tomorrow:

Bottom of the band, not the top; twelve paused reps cost far more than the percentage suggests. Limber at FITNESS: 10-8-6 burpee box jump over plus the shorter row or bike erg. Same visit, upper push and triceps — incline DB press 4 x 8-12 at 70, cable fly 3 x 12-15 at 40, lateral raise 3 x 15-20 at 20, pushdown 3 x 8-12 at 90. None of it touches the legs.

Afternoon is RT12, 55 minutes: 5' Z1, 15' Z2, 10' Z3 at 4:22-4:42/km, 20' Z2, 5' Z1. It is a tune-family code so tonight's recap analyses it automatically, but its block is half of RT19's — a threshold touch, not the retest. The classic miss is the twenty minutes afterwards: come back down to 5:01-5:45, nearer 5:20 than 5:05.

The branch, decided tonight. Signals: how the legs come out of the paused squats, whether the 15' Zone 2 lead-in feels like cruising or like work, and how the first ninety seconds of the threshold block settle.

Legs willing and the block finding its own rhythm? Run the ten minutes at the quick end of the band, 4:22-4:28/km, all ten. Legs still carrying this morning? Run the same ten minutes at the slow end, 4:38-4:42/km — same session, same duration, still genuine Zone 3. Both are a good day's work.

recapPrev.workouts:
Three pieces today, and the one that mattered was executed properly.

06:00 Cutthroat — 56' gym block, avg HR 112, max 151, load 20, RPE 5. You took 135 lb on the clean and jerks and normal wall walks rather than the light-bar [FITNESS] version I called for, plus the 60 single unders per round. Honest flag: on the lowest readiness morning of the block, that was the version with the most room to go wrong. It didn't — avg HR 112 and max 151 say you genuinely cruised it, and 21 total C&J reps at 135 sits well inside your strength. Noted, not scolded.

Arms and delts, the full Friday dose at exactly the deload loads: triceps pushdown 135 × 13, barbell curl 40 × 12, lateral raise 20 × 20. You were right about the Sorinex station — those are hamstring curls, so substituting your own barbell curls was the correct read, and the class banded face pulls covered the rear delts.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no drift signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job, and there is no fatigue flag in the trace. Confidence: high on the pace read, medium on the HR read (per-rep peaks rather than per-second plateaus).

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.
recapPrev.tomorrow:
CAn4 — 90' on the bike: 10' Z1, then 6 × (2:30 Zone 4 @ 248–283 W / 5:00 Z1), 30' Zone 2 @ 165–196 W, 5' Z1. Both bands are the post-CT31 numbers (FTP 236 W). No gym, no class — Saturday is bike only.

Coach's call, decided on tomorrow morning's numbers rather than tonight's: this is the last item on the week's list and the plan's own designated first full cut. If readiness is still down in the twenties, either drop it outright or ride only the 30' Z2 tail — six Z4 reps is the single biggest block of hard time left in a week whose entire job was to deload. If you wake up genuinely normal, ride it as written and keep the recoveries as lazy as today's were.

Sunday is full rest either way. That part isn't negotiable.

recovery.bannerTitle: RT12 — 55′ with a 10′ threshold block, and the 20 minutes afterwards are the real test
recovery.bannerSub: Two long nights back to back and the sleeping heart rate finally moving: 59 average with a nightly floor of 52, the lowest reading of the month. Readiness 48, the highest of the block. Form is still -36, so today is moderate by design rather than by permission.
recovery.note: The overnight numbers moved for the first time in three weeks and they moved in the right direction: sleeping heart rate 59 against 63 the night before, a nightly floor of 52 which is the lowest of the month, 8.1 hours asleep on top of Sunday's 8.2, breathing flat on baseline at 13.5 and wrist temperature back down to 35.8 with no illness flag. That pulls the smoothed three-night average to 61.3 against a 59.5 baseline — still above it, but half the gap it was yesterday — and readiness to 48, the highest reading of the block. The one number that has not moved is Form at -36, and today is not the day it will: this is the heaviest pure-strength leg morning of the week and a 10-minute threshold block on the same date. So the call is the plan as written with one instruction in front of it — front squats at 80 percent, not 85, because twelve reps with a three-second bottom pause cost far more than the percentage suggests, and RT12 is the session that has to survive them.

2026-08-17.mind: Yesterday I held a heart-rate ceiling for ninety minutes and it worked, and today asks for far less than that — ten unremarkable minutes at 165 watts and an hour I deliberately refuse to make interesting — because on the deepest fatigue of the block the win is that this ride costs me nothing.

cf.name: Front Squat 4×(1 pause + 2) @ 80–85% + Limber (time) — bottom of the band
cf.desc:
On the 2:30 × 4 sets: 1 pause front squat + 2 front squats @ 80–85% of 1RM front squat, plus 4 seated vertical jumps. Pause tempo = 13X1 — 1 s down, 3 s pause at the bottom, eXplode up, 1 s at the top.
Limber (for time): [TRAIN] 15-12-9 burpee box jump over 24/20 + 500/450 m row or 1000/900 m bike erg. [FITNESS]: 10-8-6 + 450/400 m row or 900/800 m bike erg.
Call: front squats at the BOTTOM of the band — 80%, not 85% — and take Limber at [FITNESS]. Against your 245 lb front squat, 80% is about 195 and 85% is about 208; across twelve paused reps that gap is not small. A 3-second pause at the bottom is far more demanding than the percentage suggests, which is the whole point of the tempo and the reason to take the lower number rather than round up.
RT12 runs later today with a 10-minute threshold block in it, and this is the heaviest pure-strength leg morning of the week. The lifting in the same visit is upper push, which touches neither.

end.name: RT12 — 55′ with a 10′ threshold block
end.desc:
5′ Zone 1 → 15′ Zone 2 @ 5:01–5:45/km → 10′ Zone 3 @ 4:22–4:42/km → 20′ Zone 2 → 5′ Zone 1. (Pulled live from the 80/20 library 16 Aug.)
RT12 is a tune-family code — tune.py names it alongside CT25, CT30 and RT16 as a session it will analyse, so the evening recap picks it up automatically. But its Zone 3 block is 10 minutes, half of RT19's 20, so treat it as a threshold touch rather than the retest. The block's scheduled retest is still week 12's CT31 and RT19.
Run the 10 minutes at genuine Zone 3 and hold it flat — steadiness is what makes a block like this readable at all. Find the effort early and stop adjusting.
The classic error is the 20 minutes afterwards. Finishing a threshold block and then running the Zone 2 tail at 4:55 turns a clean session into twenty minutes of Zone X. Come back down properly: 5:01–5:45/km, and closer to 5:20 than 5:05.
The morning is front squats at 80% with a 3-second pause, so expect the legs to feel it in the opening kilometre and give yourself the full 15′ Zone 2 to come good.

2026-08-19.mind: Six minutes of force and fourteen of Zone 4 is all the hard work this day contains, and it is the only hard work I get until Saturday — so I spend it exactly there, take the rope at whatever scale keeps my legs, and let everything either side of the reps be boringly easy.

cf.name: Snatch complex 6×1 @ 70–75% + Pinyon (AMRAP r+r) — SCALE THE DOUBLE-UNDERS
cf.desc:
On the 2:00 × 6 sets: 2 snatch pulls + 2 power snatches @ 70–75% of 1RM snatch. (1 complex = 1 rep.)
Pinyon — 4 sets of 2:00 work / 1:00 rest, picking up where you left off: [TRAIN] 9 hang power snatch 95/65 + 12 toes to bar + 60 double unders. [FITNESS]: 65/45, 12 single-leg toes to bar, 90 single unders.
Call: stay at 70% on the complex, and SCALE THE ROPE — singles, or cut the double-unders to 30. This is the one non-negotiable scale of the week and the reason is specific rather than general: 240 double-unders is a large volume of repeated jumping, and RSP18 puts seven 2-minute Zone 4 running reps on the same legs later today. That is the collision. Everything else about this morning is fine — the snatches are light, the barbell is the lightest of the week, and eight minutes of total work makes this the shortest metcon on the board.
That shortness is exactly why today carries both endurance sessions. Wednesday was chosen for the double because this class costs the least, so the saving has to be real — take it at 70% and scale the rope, and the 126 minutes of quality later today are affordable.

end.desc:

RSP18 — 5′ Z1, 5′ Zone 2, 7 × (2′ Zone 4 @ 3:48–4:17/km / 2′ Z1), 5′ Zone 2, 5′ Z1. (Pulled live from the 80/20 library 16 Aug.)
Read this one carefully, because it is not RAn4. Fourteen minutes of actual Zone 4 across seven reps — a bigger hard-run dose than anything in week 10 — and the recoveries are 2 minutes, not 5. Short rest changes the job completely: run a pace you can repeat seven times, not the fastest pace you can hold for two minutes. Aim at the slow end of the band, 4:10–4:17/km, and let rep 7 be the one that proves the pacing was right.
Leave at least four hours after the ride — later in the day, not back-to-back.
This is the first endurance session to cut all week. If Wednesday is going badly, it is the one that goes — the ride is not the thing you drop.

On the 2:00 × 6 sets: 3 pause jerks @ 70–75% of 1RM jerk.
Ponderosa — AMRAP 12: [TRAIN] 3-6-9-12… deadlifts 225/155 + 1-2-3-4… wall walks. [FITNESS]: deadlifts 155/105 + inch worm + 2 push-ups.

If the morning turns into a race, the spin cannot do its job and Saturday inherits the debt. No lifting today — all six engine targets are already complete across Tue, Wed and Thu.

60′ Zone 1 @ 118–165 W. (Pulled live from the 80/20 library 16 Aug — CRe9 is pure Zone 1 despite sitting next to CF10 in the grid row; it is NOT a Zone 2 ride.)
Pure recovery, and today it has a specific job: it is the last thing between you and CMI4.
No Zone 2 creep, no "it felt easy so I lifted it." You have the benchmark and it is a good one: last Friday's CRe10 peaked at 151 W across 75 minutes against a Zone 1 ceiling of 165, with zero seconds in Zone 2 and heart rate moving four beats across the hour. That is the standard, and it is a standard for restraint rather than for output.
This is not the day to find out what your legs have left. Tomorrow is where that question gets asked, and the answer is worth a great deal more then.
If you arrive genuinely flat, a rest day beats a recovery spin you drag yourself through — this is third in the week's cut order, behind the CrossFit intensity and Wednesday's RSP18.

2026-08-22.mind: I have ridden these intervals twice already and I know exactly what they cost, so the only genuinely new thing today is the hour of Zone 1 at the end — and riding that hour honestly, at 140 watts, when I am tired and bored and three hours in, is the actual session.

end.name: CMI4 — THE WEEK'S SESSION (180′)
end.desc:
20′ Z1 → 2 × (20′ Zone 3 @ 222–248 W / 15′ Z1) → 10 × (1′ Zone 4 @ 248–283 W / 2′ Z1) → 60′ Z1. (Pulled live from the 80/20 library 16 Aug — CMI4 is exactly CMI1 plus a 60′ Zone 1 tail; the interval content is identical to both CMI1 and CMI2.)
Nothing about the hard part is new. You have ridden this exact interval content twice: CMI1 in week 9 and CMI2 last Saturday, where block 1 went 224 W, block 2 stepped up to 235 W, and all ten Zone 4 reps held 274 W with peak heart rate flat at 154–158 across the set. The only new thing is the 60-minute Zone 1 tail — double CMI2's.
Target 222–235 W on block 1 and hold it; if heart rate plateaus clearly under 159, block 2 can go a touch firmer, exactly as it did last week. Set the effort in the first 5 minutes of each block and stop adjusting — one early correction, never a stair-step.
On-bike gate for the Zone 4 set: if you cannot get back to Zone 1 watts inside the 2′ recovery, or rep power falls below 248 W, stop the set and spin out the remainder. Ending on seven good reps is a completed session; grinding out ten bad ones is not.
The 60′ tail is Zone 1 and only Zone 1 — 118–165 W. It is the entire difference between CMI4 and CMI1, it is where a three-hour ride earns its aerobic keep, and holding 118–165 W for a full hour after two threshold blocks is a genuinely different skill from riding it fresh. Fuel it like the three-hour ride it is.
If Saturday arrives flat, slide this to Sunday and drop RF12. Never water it down into a medium ride. And if the tail specifically is what is in doubt, ride the intervals and shorten the tail — do not trade the tail for firmer intervals.

2026-08-23.mind: Ninety easy minutes the day after three hours on the bike is the hardest restraint the week asks for, and last Sunday I proved I can do it by governing heart rate instead of pace — so I run to a ceiling of 145 again and let the pace be whatever the ground decides.

end.name: RF12 — 90′ long easy run, closes the week and the block
end.desc:
5′ Z1 → 80′ Zone 2 @ 5:01–5:45/km → 5′ Z1. (Verified library structure.)
You solved this session last week and the method transfers: govern the heart rate ceiling, not the pace floor. Holding under 145 gave you 90 minutes with a maximum of 149 and zero seconds above Zone 2 by heart rate — the most disciplined long run in your file. Do that again.
Run it off the MIDDLE of the band, around 5:18–5:25/km, not the 5:01 edge. 5:01/km is a wall, not a target. If the ground tips downhill and the pace runs away at an easy heart rate, that is gravity rather than effort — do not go looking for it on purpose, and do not fight it either.
Ninety minutes of honest Zone 2 the day after 180 minutes on the bike is a hard thing to do slowly. Do it slowly — this is the taper of intensity, not of hours.
This is the day the week gives back if Saturday slid. If CMI4 moves to Sunday, this run comes out entirely.
Week 12 is the DELOAD and carries the block's retest — CT31 and RT19.
